RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Reese Delgado
Member ID: W746473340
Reference Number: POC-13C871BB40-43334
Date of Notice: 2026-08-14
Requested Service: Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
Ordering Surgeon: [Dr.] Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery, [surgeon phone/fax/NPI]

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 (lumbar laminotomy/hemilaminectomy with decompression of nerve root), issued in the above-referenced notice. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree, and the enclosed records show that an extensive, well-documented course of conservative treatment was completed without adequate relief.

1. Response to the Stated Denial Reason

The denial states that conservative treatment was not adequately documented. The clinical record submitted with the prior authorization request — and enclosed again with this appeal — shows the following conservative treatment, all completed before surgery was requested:

- Symptom duration: 9 months of progressive lower back pain, unrelieved by rest.
- Supervised physical therapy: 14 weeks (2026-04-11 through 2026-07-18), 16 completed visits, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility training, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Medication trial: NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- Interventional treatment: corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-23, which produced only 3 weeks of partial relief before symptoms returned.

Taken together, this represents a supervised, multi-modal conservative treatment course (physical therapy, medication management, and an interventional injection) sustained over several months, which failed to relieve the patient's symptoms. I ask that the reviewer identify, specifically and in writing, what element of conservative care the plan considers missing, since the duration, modalities, and outcomes are all documented in the enclosed records.

2. Correlating Clinical and Imaging Findings

In addition to the conservative-care history, the record documents objective findings supporting the medical necessity of surgical decompression:

- MRI of the lumbar spine (2026-06-22) showing an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- Functional limitation: the patient is unable to stand more than 10 minutes due to pain, with radicular pain radiating into the right calf.
- Physical examination: positive provocative testing on the affected side, with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level of nerve root compression shown on imaging.
- No active infection and no untreated substance use disorder; BMI 29; non-smoker — none of which present a contraindication to surgery.

This is a case in which the reported symptoms, physical exam findings, and imaging findings all correlate at the same spinal level (L4-L5/L5 nerve root), following a documented failure of a multi-week, multi-modal conservative treatment program.

3. Regarding the Medical Policy Cited in the Denial

The denial notice refers generally to "the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria" but does not name the specific policy, policy number, or edition applied to this request. I have been unable to independently confirm the exact wording of the specific medical-necessity criteria the plan applied to this claim. I am not quoting or attributing any specific criteria language to Anthem's policy in this appeal because I have not been able to verify that language directly from the plan's own published document — I want to be explicit that no policy text below is invented.

I am aware that Anthem's Musculoskeletal Program prior-authorization review for spine procedures, including CPT 63030, is generally performed under Carelon Medical Benefits Management's "Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines, Musculoskeletal Program – Spine Surgery" (the section addressing lumbar discectomy, foraminotomy, and laminotomy). Under the "General Clinical Guideline" section of this guideline, which I was able to retrieve and can quote directly, clinical appropriateness requires that the treating clinician "confirm the diagnosis or establish its pretest likelihood based on a complete evaluation of the patient," including "a history and physical examination and, where applicable, a review of relevant laboratory studies, diagnostic testing, and response to prior therapeutic intervention," and that "the anticipated benefit of the recommended intervention is likely to outweigh any potential harms, including from delay or decreased access to services that may result (net benefit)." The enclosed records — 9 months of symptoms, 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID use, a corticosteroid injection, correlating MRI findings, and a correlating neurologic deficit on exam — directly address each of these elements. I could not confirm the specific numeric or procedure-specific criteria (e.g., any minimum duration of therapy, required modalities, or listed exceptions) that Anthem applied in this denial, because that portion of the document was not accessible to me at the time of writing this appeal.

Accordingly, I request that Anthem:

a. Identify, in writing, the exact title, policy/document number, and edition/effective date of the medical policy or clinical guideline applied to this specific request, as required under the plan's claims and appeals procedures and applicable federal regulations (see 45 CFR 147.136), which entitle a claimant to receive, free of charge, the specific rule, guideline, protocol, or similar criterion relied upon in making an adverse benefit determination;

b. Provide the full text of the specific criteria within that document applicable to CPT 63030 / lumbar discectomy-laminotomy that the plan found was not met; and

c. Reconsider the determination in light of the conservative treatment history and correlating clinical/imaging findings documented above and in the enclosed records.

4. Enclosures

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-11 to 2026-07-18, 16 visits)
- Medication history documenting 6 months of NSAID use
- Procedure note/records for corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-23
- MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-06-22
- Office visit/exam notes documenting provocative testing and neurologic deficit
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, if available]
- [Any additional records not listed above]

5. Deadline and Requested Action

I understand that this appeal must be received by 2027-02-10, in accordance with the 180-day appeal window stated in the denial notice. I am submitting well within that deadline and request a prompt review and written determination, along with confirmation of receipt of this appeal.

If any additional information is needed to complete this review, please contact me at [phone number] or [email address], or my provider's office at [surgeon office phone/fax], and I will provide it promptly.

Thank you for your reconsideration.

Sincerely,

Reese Delgado
